shots.title: Problem and boundary
shots.screen: Synthetic Jira work item / PermitGuard title and site-procedure notice
shots.narration: In group lockout work, a permit record must not hide the people whose personal locks still protect them. PermitGuard brings that coordination into Jira. The site procedure remains authoritative.

shots.title: Identify the accepted build
shots.screen: PGSAMPLE-2 ACTIVE panel; footer 5.15.0 / UI 4e3335fb30f9; own-lock rail and top release strip
shots.narration: Here is the accepted development build and our synthetic active permit. Work-start readiness and release readiness are separate. The release blocker stays visible at the top. Historical preview is labelled; actions wait for current authorization.
shots.evidence: Owner accepted 22 Nov 21:00; capture fresh actual state

shots.title: Native Rovo, release first
shots.screen: One PermitGuard Judge; new chat: Is PGSAMPLE-2 cleared?; actual tool response
shots.narration: Ask the native Judge whether this work item is cleared. It leads with release not cleared, then gives the narrower work-start result. It reads the same deterministic service as the panel, rather than granting safety authority.
shots.evidence: Native action path accepted; not MCP transport proof

shots.title: Personal-lock release barrier
shots.screen: Explicit sample Crew B roleplay if absent; begin release checks; remove only current worker own L-A1; show L-07/V-3 blocker and blocked close
shots.narration: For this synthetic exercise, Crew B is explicitly simulated. I begin release checks and remove only my own lock. A remaining shared-equipment personal-lock record still blocks release and closure. This is not another real worker, and not permission to remove someone else’s lock.
shots.evidence: Record only after human preflight/approval; no mutations by documentation task

shots.title: Authorized reread in another tab
shots.screen: Actual second-tab update if captured; otherwise manually Refresh with visible label
shots.narration: The other tab reads authorized state again. Realtime carries only invalidation hints, not permit records or safety authority. Refresh remains the fallback.
shots.evidence: Only claim delivery if visible in recorded run; no fixed latency claim

shots.title: Human-only activation boundary
shots.screen: Source/README action diagram: GET readiness, CREATE PENDING, no agent confirmation tool
shots.narration: The agent has no confirmation tool. Its activation action can only propose pending work for a named human. Equipment confirmation remains human-only; a QR or photo does not independently prove presence.
shots.evidence: Implemented/local-tested rule; not a new live activation demonstration

shots.title: MCP evidence — gated alternate
shots.screen: DEFAULT: manifest tools and MCP readiness matrix with pending label. VERIFIED ALTERNATE: approved Studio/client discovery and real read-only tool receipt, only after audit is signed off.
shots.narration: The same actions are declared as Forge MCP tools. Native Judge use alone does not prove MCP discovery. Today the authenticated MCP route and official bonus wording still need verification, so this is architecture evidence, not a claim that the bonus is complete.
shots.evidence: Default unverified branch; replace only after authenticated receipt and rules match

shots.title: Architecture and close
shots.screen: README architecture, public MIT repository and remaining release blocker
shots.narration: Forge stores bounded records and checks revisions before writes. Jira access remains user-authorized. No external app runtime or SQL is needed. Named humans and the site procedure remain in control.
